svg.title: Enterprise–resident public decision ledger
svg.desc: Keep the public question, synthetic screen, authorised input, accountable owner, decision state, response receipt and fallback in one reviewable chain.
svg.text: Keep the public question, synthetic screen, authorised input, accountable owner, decision state, response receipt and fallback in one reviewable chain.

g.text: PUBLIC QUESTION
record the question and boundary first
SYNTHETIC SCREEN
mark conflicts for later checking
AUTHORISED INPUT
an authorised owner opens the window
RESPONSE RECEIPT

svg.text: EIGHT QUESTION ENTRANCES · ONE FIELD SET · ONE PAUSE AND FALLBACK CHAIN

g.text: PDL-01 · RESIDENT DAILY
Do daily trips break at transfer points
SYNTHETIC SCREEN
The synthetic network marks possible transfer breaks and alter
natives; it is not resident experience
AUTHORISED INPUT
Dated time-binned mode counts, service-point walkthrough, raw
complaint register and authorised grouped input
PAUSE
Pause when the daily route is cut, no human equivalent exists
or the response receipt is missing · Ordinary rail and bus, st
affed desk, phone and paper route
PDL-02 · CARE AND ACCESSIBILITY
Can care trips and accessible continuity hold
SYNTHETIC SCREEN
The synthetic pressure screen finds route and resource conflic
ts; it is not an accessibility walkthrough
AUTHORISED INPUT
Continuous-route walkthrough, ramp and lift status, carer part
icipation, human takeover record and independent review
PAUSE
Pause when a route is blocked, the alternative is inaccessible
or independent review is absent · Human guidance, ordinary pu
blic transport and removable temporary facilities
PDL-03 · ENTERPRISE ARRIVAL
Do enterprise windows displace public space
SYNTHETIC SCREEN
Synthetic scenarios compare time-window conflict and fallback
order; they do not prove that shuttles reduce cars
AUTHORISED INPUT
Grouped enterprise demand, schedules and vehicle classes, righ
t-of-way records, fire-clearance check and employee mode count
s
PAUSE
Pause when enterprise priority displaces resident, accessible
or fire access or lacks a guaranteed-home fallback · Ordinary
public transport, human dispatch, cancelled curb booking and g
uaranteed-home arrangement
PDL-04 · CURB AND MAINTENANCE
Who owns conflict, clearing and response
SYNTHETIC SCREEN
The synthetic curb ledger checks responsibility and conflict f
ields; it does not prove staffing
AUTHORISED INPUT
Curb ownership, maintenance roster, event log, complaint ticke
ts, response times and escalation route
PAUSE
Pause when the owner, clearing route or complaint status is mi
ssing · Close automated booking and use the staffed desk and o
rdinary public transport
PDL-05 · TRANSFER PASSENGER
Can rail, bus, bicycle and walking connect
SYNTHETIC SCREEN
The synthetic network checks transfer chains and breaks; it is
not station demand or accessibility performance
AUTHORISED INPUT
Time-binned station flows, transfer counts, bicycle parking, a
ccessibility walkthrough and public-wayfinding check
PAUSE
Pause when the transfer chain breaks, human access disappears
or the emergency route is discontinuous · Ordinary rail and bu
s plus staffed station guidance
PDL-06 · EXTERNAL COMMUTE
Are external commute costs and fallbacks visible
SYNTHETIC SCREEN
Synthetic OD compares path, time-window and mode conflicts; it
is not observed external inflow
AUTHORISED INPUT
De-identified grouped OD, external operator coordination, park
-and-ride counts and cross-owner response receipt
PAUSE
Pause when external data are unexplained, cross-owner takeover
is absent or ground fallback breaks · Ordinary rail and bus,
public transfer information and staffed desk
PDL-07 · NIGHT WORK AND RETURN
Do safe human choices remain at night
SYNTHETIC SCREEN
The synthetic time-window screen flags last-service and fallba
ck conflicts; it is not night safety evidence
AUTHORISED INPUT
Night-time walkthrough, last-service information, lighting and
help-point check, incident and complaint register
PAUSE
Pause when no public or human-equivalent route remains after l
ast service or incidents lack escalation · Ordinary public tra
nsport, staffed desk, phone help and withdrawn automated servi
ce
PDL-08 · FREIGHT, EMERGENCY AND MAINTENANCE
Can loading, fire access and maintenance coexist
SYNTHETIC SCREEN
Synthetic curb pressure exposes conflict combinations and with
drawal order; it is not field availability
AUTHORISED INPUT
Vehicle classes, loading windows, fire and emergency check, ma
intenance roster and event replay
PAUSE
Pause when fire clearance, resident passage or maintenance fal
lback cannot be guaranteed · Close the experimental window and
use ordinary public routes and human field dispatch

svg.text: Only the decision chain is reviewable. Field status, resident input, public support, operating permission and transport performance remain unknown.
